posts.author: RavenBlueIndigo
posts.body:
Hello!
I'm in need of a plugin that inserts a small delay between selecting choices in order to prevent accidentally speeding through another choice. I'd like the delay length to be customizable.
Many thanks to anyone that can handle this~
. . . Also, a question for any coders that may view this . . . I didn't make it the main topic of this thread, but I have some show text commands that are meant to persist visibly across multiple show choice branches, and so I handle that by extra show text copies using the \> command. However, I've noticed that if the text goes onto a second row, there is a visible flicker in that row that I assume is the engine taking an extra frame to load it. Would it be possible to somehow make it immediately load flawlessly? If it is a simple fix and not too much to ask, I'd also like that handled, but the choice delay takes priority.

As for what I mean by it persisting is that this is mainly for an evented combat system, and it has text like
"The enemy stands before you. It is Hadrian's turn."
And, then you can select your skills by going through different choices. I want the aforementioned text to show at all times, which requires me to make copies of it above other choice branches, and to make them load immediately, I have to use \>, but all rows beyond the first flicker briefly between choice entries, and I wanted to know if that was addressable. It's not really an issue that I can take a screenshot of. It'd require a video.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
RavenBlueIndigo said:
Because adding a wait command would make the choices disappear briefly
Click to expand...
Why? The choice window closes as soon as you select something, so it's already disappearing. You would put a Wait command before showing it again so that the player's keystroke to close a Show Text or whatever doesn't register in the next choice window.
You can also just set your Show Choices to have no default, which means the player must move with the arrow keys or mouse to select an option - just pressing confirm will have no effect.
RavenBlueIndigo said:
It's not really an issue that I can take a screenshot of.
Click to expand...
Of course it is. You open up the event in the editor and press Print Screen. That way, whether or not the issue is immediately visible to people who are proficient with eventing, they can duplicate it in their own test game to see. But you insist on giving nothing instead
RavenBlueIndigo said:
It'd require a video.
Click to expand...
If you like - that's not terribly difficult to do, either. But I think most people who would try to help you would prefer to simply have the event so it's easy for them to change things and try fixes.
